SE to schedule infra checklist call and perf benchmark window (Nina) - due 2025-03-17
BetaHealth to confirm pilot dataset and success metrics (James) - due 2025-03-19

Nina: Send infra checklist + request for vpc peering details (due 2025-03-17)

header: Attendees (Redwood): Maya Chen (AE), Diego Alvarez (CSM), Nina Patel (SE)
Attendees (BetaHealth): James Foster (Head of ML), Aisha Rahman (Platform Lead), Liam O'Connor (Security)
summary: Onboarding kickoff for BetaHealth's pilot of Redwood Inference. Objectives: align on pilot scope, timeline, success metrics, infra access (VPC/private), and security requirements. Agreement to run a 4-week pilot using Redwood Dedicated capacity with a baseline perf window for latency/cost measurement.

Key risks discussed: data residency and encryption KMS, timeline for VPC peering, and expected throughput for peak hours. Plan: SE-led infra checklist and perf benchmark in week 1, orientation and evals in week 2-3, roll to staging by week 4.
transcript: [00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about 45, 50 minutes, quick intros?
[00:08] James: James Foster, head of ML at BetaHealth, good to meet you all
[00:11] Aisha: Aisha, Platform Lead, I'll own the infra side
[00:14] Liam: Liam, security, I'll be asking about KMS and logs
[00:18] Maya: Great, Redwood side we have me Maya AE, Diego our CSM, and Nina our solutions engineer
[00:25] Diego: Hi all, excited to kick off, want to get alignment on scope and timeline and what success looks like
[01:02] Nina: I'll walk through the infra checklist and perf benchmarks later, but first can you outline the pilot workload James?

[01:15] James: Sure, we're evaluating inference for clinical notes summarization and triage routing, roughly 30 qps peak during batch windows, average request length 350 tokens, sometimes up to 1k tokens
[01:40] Aisha: Important for us is data residency; we need logs and data to stay in US regions, also KMS for encryption at rest
[01:55] Liam: SOC2 is a must, also audit trail for access, and MFA for console access
[02:10] Maya: Totally, we have a SOC2 package and can share our audit docs, we also support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments
[02:35] James: For pilot, do you recommend hosted or dedicated?

[02:40] Nina: For predictable latency and to simulate production we usually recommend Dedicated, especially with the throughput you mentioned, Dedicated also gets you isolation and predictable batch windows
[02:58] James: Cost tradeoffs?
[03:02] Maya: There's a pricing delta, dedicated has a monthly commit but lowers per-token unit cost at scale; we'll send a dedicated vs hosted comparison sheet
[03:20] Aisha: We will likely need VPC peering, can you support VPC peering and private IPs?
[03:28] Nina: Yes, Private deployment supports VPC peering, and for Dedicated we can do private endpoints, we'll need network ranges and a contact at your networking team
[03:50] Liam: On KMS, can you integrate with our AWS KMS/HSM?
[03:55] Nina: We support customer KMS for the Private control plane; for Dedicated we can enable encryption using your KMS — we'll document exact steps in the infra checklist
[04:20] Diego: On timeline, are you aiming to be live in production or just pilot?
[04:25] James: Pilot first, goal to be in staging in ~4 weeks, and production later in Q2 if pilot meets SLA
[04:40] Maya: Sounds good, typical onboarding timeline is infra and benchmarks week 1, integration and evals week 2-3, staging handoff week 4
[05:05] James: We need to define success metrics — latency p95 under 200ms and cost per 1k tokens under our threshold
[05:20] Nina: We'll run a perf window where we replay your sample traffic for an hour to get realistic metrics; we'll need a sample dataset and a small harness
[05:45] James: I'll coordinate sample data access, probably synthetic obfuscated notes to meet privacy
[06:00] Aisha: How do you handle logs retention and who can see them?

[06:05] Diego: By default logs are accessible in the console to users with RBAC, for Private we can restrict access and we retain logs per your retention policy — we'll include options in the security doc
[06:25] Liam: Do you keep user prompts in logs? We need to avoid PII retention unless explicitly allowed
[06:32] Maya: Right, we have redaction options and promise we don't use customer prompts for model training; will provide the DPA and security FAQ
[06:55] James: Are there any known performance regressions with quantized models? We want predictable quality
[07:02] Nina: We recommend specific quantization profiles per model; we'll include model/quantization recommendations based on your token distribution and quality targets
[07:25] Aisha: On deployment, do you support canary or A/B rollouts?
[07:30] Maya: Yes, Redwood supports canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies so you can test new versions safely
[07:45] James: Any prebuilt SDKs? We prefer python and node
[07:49] Diego: We have Python and Node SDKs and REST API, plus examples for streaming and tool-calling
[08:10] Nina: For the perf benchmark we'll need to know typical sequence length, request distribution and concurrency — you mentioned 30 qps peak but burstiness matters
[08:30] James: Peak bursts can be 60 qps for short intervals during morning syncs
[08:38] Nina: Good to know, will size batchers accordingly, and determine if autoscaling/burst capacity is needed
[08:55] Aisha: Network constraints: we have strict egress rules, can you work with a transit VPC?
[09:00] Nina: Yes, we have experience with transit VPCs and can set up whitelisted endpoints, we'll detail the network ports and IP ranges in the checklist
[09:18] Liam: For audit we need SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning
[09:23] Maya: We support SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM for user provisioning, we'll include SSO config in the onboarding doc
[09:40] James: Who will be our main POC from Redwood during the pilot?
[09:44] Diego: I'll be primary CSM contact and Nina is the lead SE for technical tasks, Maya for commercial questions
[10:05] Maya: We'll also share a welcome packet with links: onboarding doc, security package, perf spreadsheet
[10:22] James: Can you share the perf spreadsheet template?
[10:25] Nina: Yes, we'll attach a benchmark sheet with columns for p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, and config used
[11:00] Aisha: On data residency, we need to ensure processing stays in US east region for now
[11:06] Nina: We'll pin the region for the Dedicated pool and note any fallbacks; smart routing won't route out of the pinned region unless explicitly allowed
[11:30] Liam: Encryption in transit — TLS?
[11:33] Maya: All traffic is TLS 1.2+, mTLS for private endpoints can be enabled
[11:55] James: Any compliance artifacts for healthcare?
[11:58] Diego: We have SOC2 reports and a HIPAA-facing addendum for enterprise plans; we'll check legal for specifics and share an outline
[12:20] Aisha: Integration point — we plan to call Redwood from our inference host inside our VPC, will you support direct private endpoints?
[12:28] Nina: Yes, dedicated private endpoints are supported, we'll need CIDR and an owner to schedule peering
[12:45] James: For evaluation, can we run A/B against our in-house model?
[12:50] Nina: Absolutely, Redwood supports routing policies so you can split traffic between variants
[13:05] Maya: Let's talk timeline concretely — Diego, can you propose a week-by-week plan?
[13:10] Diego: Week 1: infra checklist + perf window. Week 2: integration work and initial evals. Week 3: iterate prompts and quantization. Week 4: staging handoff and production runbook
[13:30] James: That aligns with our internal milestones, we need executive update at end of pilot
[13:38] Maya: We'll provide a short exec summary template you can reuse
[13:50] Liam: On logging detail — can we restrict transcript log access to specific roles?
[13:55] Diego: Yes, RBAC can restrict who sees raw prompts and who sees aggregated metrics
[14:12] Aisha: Are there known integrations for observability? We use Datadog
[14:17] Nina: We can forward metrics to Datadog and provide per-route dashboards in the Redwood Console
[14:40] James: Any blockers you foresee?
[14:44] Nina: Biggest potential blockers are network peering delays and legal review on the DPA/KMS — both typical and manageable
[15:05] Maya: We'll aim to get you the security package and DPA draft by Friday
[15:11] James: Sounds good, we'll loop in legal and infra owners once we get that
[15:25] Aisha: For the perf window, do you need us to run traffic from our side or can Redwood replay?
[15:31] Nina: Both options are fine — replaying on Redwood side is simplest, but if you prefer origin traffic we can coordinate a traffic mirror
[15:50] James: We'll likely opt for replay with synthetic data for privacy
[16:00] Diego: I'll follow up with calendar invites for the infra call and perf window, Nina will send the checklist

[16:15] Maya: Quick recap — action items and owners, security package and pricing by Maya, infra checklist and perf schedule by Nina, CSM timeline by Diego, BetaHealth to provide sample data and CIDR info
[16:32] James: Great, thanks everyone, looking forward to it
[16:35] Maya: Thanks all, we'll send notes and next steps in the next 24 hours
[16:40] (end of recording)
